description: Cloudy, but drinkable, if you're desperate enough.
Threaded bones on a cord. Sells for a little, means nothing on its own.
A trophy, if you want to call it that.
Warm, even out of the water. Something about it feels like it's still listening.
Pulled hot from the transformer room the moment it drained. Still holds a charge.
A waterproofed recording, timestamped weeks before the flood. Proof the canal locks were sealed on purpose.
A torn tag, still readable: STALL 7B - EXOTIC IMPORTS.
Still ticking, somehow. Kru Viroj would want this back.
Warm to the touch. Actually blessed, unlike most of what's sold here.
Shipping records for "biological samples," routed from a trench off the coast, dated days before the first fissure broke.
Prices in a currency nobody uses anymore, for goods that were never for sale.
Still warm. Still faintly singing, off-key.
Thicker than it should be, and warm on the underside.
Laminate long gone. The name underneath is still legible, if you want to know it.
Salvaged from the sluice crane's console. Still holds a charge.
Handwritten shipping ledgers. Ratchaprasong elites, trading food for children - fuel or sacrifice, the entries don't say which.
Still humming faintly with residual hydraulic pressure.
Dense, black, and warm. It beats, slowly, if you hold it long enough to notice.
Laminated, waterlogged, still humming faintly when it's near a working reader. Someone's lanyard, once.
Pulled off something that used to have hands. The teeth are half rusted through, but it still turns.
Too heavy for its size, and it never quite dries. Whatever wore this ring outranked the flood itself.
Salvaged medical kit, somehow still sterile. Whoever packed it wanted someone to survive.
Small, brass, still warm - like it was just made rather than found.
Stamped with a stall number that doesn't match anything on the market map anymore.
It tracks you around the room even packed away in a bag. Worth a fortune to the cult, which is exactly why you're taking it.
Salvaged from the Vivarium's medical stock, somehow still viable. Whatever it was made for, it works on you too.
Weatherproofed and still magnetic-striped. Somebody cared enough about Stack-City to laminate this.
Heavier than a key needs to be, stamped with a shipping line's logo nobody's used in years.
Fused shell and rust in a rough circle. It was never meant to be worn, and it doesn't care.
The seal held. Whatever's inside is decades past its date and still better than nothing.
